out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in THE THREE-VAT SINK AT THE COFFEE STATION.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. CDI: EMPLOYEE RE-EDUCATED AND WASHED HIS HANDS IN HANDWASHING SINK.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: OBSERVED COFFEE MACHINE EQUIPMENT RINSED BUT NOT WASHED NOR SANITIZED AT THREE-VAT SINK IN COFFEE AREA.. OBSERVED PLATES, BOWLS, CUPS, AND UTENSILS IN SANITIZER VAT OF THREE-VAT SINK IN KITCHEN WITH SANITIZER AT ~0PPM QUAT.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. CDI: QUAT SANITIZER OF ~200PPM MADE AND ALL ITEMS LISTED ABOVE WERE WASHED, RINSED, AND SANITIZED.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food
violations.observation: A review of the menu with the foodservice operator indicates that there is no consumer advisory for the following food item(s) that may be served raw and/or undercooked: OBSERVED NO CONSUMER ADVISORY FOR KITFO AND DULET DISHES ON MENU AND THEY WERE LISTED AS ABLE TO BE SERVED UNDERCOOKED.
violations.corrective_action: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw or undercooked the permit holder shall inform consumers of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. ADD THE CONSUMER ADVISORY TO ALL MENUS BY MARCH 26. PLEASE SEND PHOTOS OF CORRECTED MENU.

violations.title: Ceasing Operations & Reporting (Voluntary for Imminent Health Hazard)
violations.observation: The permit holder failed to discontinue operations and notify the Health Department that an imminent health hazard may exist because of an emergency. IMMINENT HEALTH HAZARD OBSERVED (RODENT INFESTATION AND FECES ON FOOD, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES, NON-FOOD CONTACT SURFACES)
violations.corrective_action: CDI: OWNER VOLUNTARILY CLOSED RESTAURANT/COFFEE SHOP. RESTAURANT/COFFEE SHOP MAY NOT OPERATE (INCLUDING PREPARING FOOD) UNTIL IT IS APPROVED TO RE-OPEN BY A REPRESENTATIVE OF FAIRFAX COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT. MARKET IS ALLOWED TO OPERATE. out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. OBSERVED NO PAPER TOWELS AVAILABLE AT HANDWASHING SINK NEAR THREE-VAT SINK.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. OBSERVED NO HAND SOAP PROVIDED AT HANDWASHING SINK NEAR THREE-VAT SINK.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: OBSERVED SANITIZER BUCKET AND WIPING CLOTHS IN THE HANDWASHING SINK NEAR THE THREE-VAT SINK.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. CDI: ITEMS REMOVED FROM SINK.

out_items.name: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated

violations.title: Safe, Unadulterated & Honestly Presented
violations.observation: -OBSERVED MOUSE DROPPINGS IN ENJIRA DOUGH IN BUCKET ON FLOOR OF KITCHEN. -OBSERVED MOUSE DROPPINGS ON FLOUR IN FLOUR BAG. -OBSERVED MOUSE DROPPINGS IN DEHYDRATED BEEF.
violations.corrective_action: CDI: ALL OF THE ABOVE FOODS WERE THROWN AWAY. IF ANY OTHER FOOD PACKAGE OR FOOD IS FOUND TO HAVE MOUSE DROPPINGS OR CHEWING, IT MUST BE DISPOSED OF.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: IN TWO DOOR STAND-UP (NEAR MIXER) OBSERVED RAW SHELLED EGGS ON TOP OF RTE BREAD. IN ONE-DOOR STAND-UP COOLER (ACROSS FROM THREE-VAT) OBSERVED RAW BEEF ON TOP OF RAW VEGETABLES AND VARIOUS OTHER RTE FOODS.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. OWNER RE-EDUCATED AND FACILITY SELF-CLOSED DUE TO INFESTATION. OWNER UNDERSTANDS COOLERS WILL BE ORGANIZED BEFORE EHS RETURNS TO RE-OPEN FACILITY.

violations.title: Cover Foods in Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped or uncovered food in the following location where the food is subject to contamination: OBSERVED MANY LARGE BAGS OF DRY FOODS SUCH AS FLOUR, SPICES, AND LENTILS.
violations.corrective_action: Foods shall be protected from contamination by being stored in packages, covered containers or wrappings unless being cooled. ALL BAGGED ITEMS MUST BE PLACED IN TOTES TO PROTECT FROM RODENTS AND OTHER CONTAMINANTS. ANY ITEMS FOUND TO HAVE SIGNS OF PESTS (FECES, CHEWING) MUST BE DISPOSED OF.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Food Contact Surfaces Clean to Sight & Touch
violations.observation: The following equipment/utensils were observed soiled to sight and touch: OBSERVED SERVING PLATES, METAL LIDS, FLOOR MIXER, AND OTHER FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES TO HAVE MOUSE DROPPINGS ON THEM.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to the sight and touch. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. ALL FOOD CONTACT SURFACES IN FACILITY MUST BE WASHED, RINSED, AND SANITIZED BEFORE USING THEM FOR ANY PURPOSE.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: -HOMEMADE UNSALTED BUTTER IN BUCKET ON FLOOR OF KITCHEN OBSERVED AT ~70F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: BUTTER THROWN AWAY.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED NO DATE MARKING ON FOOD CONTAINERS IN FACILITY.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: LENTIL SAMBOSAS
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. CDI: PIC THREW SAMBOSAS AWAY. Heber Market & Cafe (Inspection Date: 09/17/2025) Page 3 of 5

out_items.name: Compliance with variance, specialized process, HACCP

violations.title: Variance Requirement, Health Department Determines Need
violations.observation: OBSERVED MULTIPLE BINS BEING USED TO FERMENT DOUGH AT ROOM TEMPERATURE TO MAKE INJIRA. OWNER STATED FERMENTING AT ROOM TEMPERATURE LASTS FOR THREE DAYS.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall obtain a variance from the Regulatory Authority as specified in 8-103.10 and under 8-103.11 before: 1. smoking food as a method of food preservation rather than as a method for flavor enhancement, 2. curing food, 3. using food additives or adding components such as vinegar, 4. packaging food using a Reduced Oxygen Packaging method, 5. operating a molluscan shellfish life-support system display tank used to store and display shellfish that are offered for human consumption, 6. custom processing animals that are for personal use as food and not for sale or service in a food establishment, 7. preparing food by another method that is determined by the Regularty Authority to require a variance or, 8. sprouting seeds or beans. CDI: OWNER AWARE ALL DOUGH MUST BE DISPOSED OF AND NOT FOR SERVING TO THE PUBLIC. OWNER AWARE HE MAY STORE DOUGH AT 41F OR BELOW FOR 6 DAYS. ONCE COOKED, HOMEMADE INJIRA MUST BE STORED AT 135F OR ABOVE OR 41F OR BELOW FOR A MAXIMUM OF 6 DAYS.

violations.title: Variance Requirement, Curing Food
violations.observation: The person in charge described a specialized processing method of food preservation requiring a variance from the Health Department is used for the following meat, fish, poultry, game animal, or ratite product: OBSERVED FACILITY TO BE DEHYDRATING STRIPS OF BEEF IN A DEHYDRATOR AND STORING WITHOUT TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR AN UNLIMITED AMOUNT OF TIME.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall obtain a variance from the Regulatory Authority as specified in 8-103.10 and under 8-103.11 before: 1) smoking food as a method of food preservation rather than as a method for flavor enhancement, 2) curing food, 3) using food additives or adding components such as vinegar, 4) packaging food using a Reduced Oxygen Packaging method, 5) operating a molluscan shellfish life-support system display tank used to store and display shellfish that are offered for human consumption, 6) custom processing animals that are for personal use as food and not for sale or service in a food establishment, 7) preparing food by another method that is determined by the Regulatory Authority to require a variance, or 8) sprouting seeds or beans. CDI: OWNER AGREED TO REMOVE DEHYDRATOR FROM FACILITY THIS EVENING. EHS DIRECTED OWNER THAT HE CAN BAKE THE BEEF THEN KEEP UNDER TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR A MAXIMUM OF 6 DAYS.

violations.title: HACCP Plan Required by Law
violations.observation: A HACCP Plan was not submitted prior to engaging in FERMENTING INJIRA DOUGH AT ROOM TEMPERATURE AND DEHYDRATING BEEF.
violations.corrective_action: CDI: OWNER AGREED TO UTILIZE TEMPERATURE CONTROL AND ONLY KEEP ITEMS FOR A MAXIMUM OF 6 DAYS. OWNER AWARE HE MUST SUBMIT VARIANCE AND HACCP APPLICATION AND HAVE APPLICATIONS APPROVED BEFORE DEHYDRATING BEEF AND FERMENTING INJIRA DOUGH AT ROOM TEMPERATURE.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

OWNER MUST FOLLOW WHAT PEST CONTROL COMPANY ADVISES IN ORDER TO END THE INFESTATION AND ELIMINATE HARBORAGE CONDITIONS.

violations.observation: Harborage conditions exist.

violations.observation: OBSERVED HOMEMADE UNSALTED BUTTER STORED IN A HOME DEPOT 5GAL BUCKET. OBSERVED TRASH BINS USED TO STORE FOODS THROUGHOUT FACILITY.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.'
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS PROVIDED DOCUMENT.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS PROVIDED DOCUMENT.
